title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation Could Have One Of The Biggest Download Sizes In Xbox History
text: Final Fantasy VII Revelation Could Have One Of The Biggest Download Sizes In Xbox History | Pure Xbox Menu Search Share Guest Guest Login | Sign Up Pure Xbox News Reviews Features Games Guides Videos Forums Search Keywords Guest Login or Sign Up Home Choose Topics... Manage Topics News Xbox Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Xbox Series X Xbox Series S Final Fantasy VII Revelation Could Have One Of The Biggest Download Sizes In Xbox History Just to warn you by Fraser Gilbert 6 hours ago Share: The next few months are going to be painful for Xbox storage space, folks. Not only have we got the likes of GTA 6 and Fable on the way, which are surely going to be well over the 100GB mark (and the rest), but the director of Final Fantasy VII Revelation has also suggested it's going to have one of the biggest download sizes in Xbox history. According to Naoki Hamaguchi in a new interview with VGC , Final Fantasy VII Revelation will be around the 200GB mark when it launches in April of 2027, which explains why it can't ship entirely on one or even two discs. He nevertheless says that delivering "some kind of physical product" remains important to the team: "Things are still getting worked out, but it’s probably going to be around 200GB of game. I understand there are a lot of opinions about this topic, but at the end of the day, the fact is we need to overcome the hardware to a certain extent. One thing I want to say is, even though the game will not be on the full disc, in the position we’re in, because discs may be dying out, or maybe staying, with Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, we definitely wanted to deliver some kind of physical product. That was really important to us. Trust me!" Assuming they aren't able to bring the download size down, FFVII Revelation will find itself in the company of games from the likes of Call of Duty , ARK , NBA 2K and various others that are packing huge download and install sizes. It's not a massive deal for Xbox Series X owners who can fit a bunch of games on their console at once, but Xbox Series S owners who want to play all of these big hitters in 2027 will have to do some thinking - either delete their games and reinstall them as necessary, or perhaps consider an Xbox Expansion Card to boost their free space. We'll cross that bridge when we get to it, eh? For now, we're just excited to finally finish the FF7 remake trilogy next year! But on a the series s I could see this being a massive headache. 0 6 BAMozzy 5 hours ago @Nakatomi_Uk It doesn't matter what the 'highest' capacity discs that they make, its thev highest capacity of discs the drive can read that matters and the Xbox doesn't have the highest capacity for gaming use - I believe its 50GB dual layer discs for Cross-Gen Compatibility: Sticking with 50GB capacities allows Microsoft to use a single unified disc SKU that works across both the Xbox One and the Xbox Series X via Smart Delivery (what I could find about it) The 'more' discs, the more it costs to manufacture and ship, increasing the number of copies a game must sell to become profitable and justify the costs of making all the parts, case, cover, discs, etc and sealed, the extra weight adds to shipping costs etc and the disc is purely a delivery method to get the 'licence' to the Customer. The 'software' doesn't run from disc so doesn't matter if none, some or all of the game code is distributed on disc - it has to be downloaded and installed on the SSD to be playable, to 'function' as discs/disc drives are far to slow for modern games to run. Games haven't run from disc since the 360 era and have required installation on internal storage. With games now designed around the data transfer speeds of SSD's to ensure Loading and texture streaming are virtually instantaneous instead of minutes, the only reason you put a disc in the slot is to prove you still own the licence to play, the key to unlock access to the software on your hardware. Virtually ALL games require internet downloads because the code they do supply is the 'beta' code, the pre-release version they had to send to the manufacturer months before to put 'something' on the disc that they can update to version 1.0 (or better) on Day 1 and then add the rest of the content, fix the other bugs/glitches the community of gamers encounter etc. With only 50GB Capacity, they certainly will rely on Online to distribute the rest of the Software. The point of a disc is to 'distribute' a Physical Licence that you can sell or lend to a friend, but unlike the 360 (or earlier) days, you've not been able to put physical media into the hardware and play that game without installing it first and often requiring updates too. 0 7 Mr-Cage 4 hours ago @Balaam_ Is there any kind of gaming news that you don't react negatively to? 5 8 Coletrain 4 hours ago I'll make sure I've got room spare.
